frontMatter.welcome:
Welcome to Arrival Fashion Ltd.!!!
We are thrilled to welcome you to the Arrival Fashion Ltd. (AFL) family and wish you every success in your journey with us!
We believe that every employee plays an integral role in AFL’s growth and success, and we hope that you will take pride in becoming a valued member of our team.
As you embark on this new chapter, you will encounter various training sessions and new processes. While there may be a lot to absorb initially, please remember to take a moment to review our core values: Care, Integrity, and Excellence. These values are the foundation of our work culture and will be essential to your success at Arrival Fashion Ltd. and in your overall career. Let them guide your actions and decisions as you become part of our dynamic team.
This handbook has been created to help you understand what we expect from our employees, and it also outlines the policies, programs, and benefits available to eligible team members. We encourage you to familiarize yourself with the contents of the handbook as soon as possible, as it will provide answers to many of the questions you may have about working with AFL.

chapters.title: Social Accountability Policy
chapters.text:
Arrival Fashion Ltd. is committed to protect worker’s right and improve labour conditions and social performance within the organisation and in all its stakeholder partnership and relationships.
Arrival Fashion Ltd. is committed to comply with local national and all other applicable laws and prevailing industry standards.
- Child Labour: AFL, since inception has followed the practice of not engaging workers who are less than 18 years of age in its workforce.
- Forced of compulsory Labour: AFL does not engage or support the use of forced or compulsory labour. It promotes an environment for the workforce to work voluntarily, without any threat of punishment or retaliation.
- Health & Safety: AFL is committed to providing healthy and safe working environment for all personnel employed or contracted.
- Freedom Of Association: AFL respects and supports the right to freedom of association and ensures that workers and their organizations are not subjected to any discrimination at workplace.
- Non-Discrimination: In consonance with code of conduct, AFL provides an equal opportunity to all the employees and qualified applicants for employment without discrimination of any kind. AFL exercises positive discrimination in favour of socially disadvantaged communities, provided potential employees fulfil their merit-based criteria.
- Disciplinary Practice: AFL has always treated and will treat all its personnel with dignity and respect. All disciplinary actions are in accordance with law.
- Security Practices: The security of AFL is practiced ensuring due consideration of human rights under all circumstances.
- Working Hours: AFL complies with all applicable laws and industry standards on working hours.
- Compensation Practices: AFL ensures that its workforce is paid wages which meet or exceed the minimum wage as per law.
- Supply Chain Practices: AFL promotes human rights practices in its supply chain through various engagement forums, training, surveys, third party audits and its inclusion as a criterion in vendor registration process.
- Management System: The Company continuously tracks its human rights and social performance through establishing effective management system. Any complaint or grievance is addressed judiciously and used as input to further improve the system and processes.
- Collective Bargaining: Worker have rights to join the collective bargaining Organization.
- Young Worker: Arrival Fashion since inception has followed the practice of not engaging workers who are less than 18 years of age in its workforce. Not engaging young worker in premises.
- NGO Agreements: Organization will do agreement with NGO to handle such cases. Arrival Fashion Ltd proactively enters into agreements with non-governmental organizations to handle pertinent cases, reinforcing its dedication to ethical and socially responsible practices. In summary, Arrival Fashion Ltd is resolute in fostering an environment of fairness, respect, and social accountability, where the rights and well-being of its workforce are upheld as paramount.
## Quality, Environment, Health & Safety Policy
- Arrival Fashion Ltd. is one of the most respected apparel manufacturing companies in Bangladesh’s private sector. We are committed to enhancing customer satisfaction by consistently delivering high-quality products that meet both current and future fashion needs. Our dedication extends to continuously improving environmental, health, and safety standards across our processes, products, and services.
We are also committed to:
- Comply with applicable legal & other requirements related to quality, environment, health & safety.
## Protect the environment and prevent environmental pollution by
- Reducing and conserving the use of natural resources like electricity, water, steam etc. wherever possible
- Reduce / recycle / reuse of waste wherever possible.
- Reducing local pollution and impact on biodiversity through adopting latest technology / monitoring, measuring, and controlling the impact of local environmental pollution.
- implement a product life cycle approach across the entire supply chain.
- No complaint from external stakeholder from operational environment.
- Provide safe and healthy working condition for the prevention of work-related injury & ill health of all interested parties by
- Eliminating and controlling health and safety hazards and its risk by regular medical checkup, inspection of safety equipment, providing suitable PPE at workplace, condition monitoring of workplace etc.
- Enhancing awareness of workplace safety through training, communication, motivation, and their consultation & participation where they exist.
- Control and eliminate business and process risk; and seize opportunities.
- Define and communicate the objectives, targets & its strategy to achieve them to ensure the adequacy of the necessary resources.
- Adopting and promoting process approach and risk base thinking concept among the organization.

## Compensation and Annual Revision Policy
The Compensation & Benefit structure is critical for the Company and will influence our ability to compete for talent over the short, medium, and long term. Since we are a growing company in Bangladesh, to succeed, our organization must gain and maintain an edge over its competitors, that is, our organization must develop a competitive advantage or superior marketplace position relative to our competitors. Employees are the key Assets for competitive advantage in the global market today. Hence, we may conclude that Competitive advantage can accrue to an organization when the employees are managed effectively. Since Compensation is the prime source of attracting and retaining Talent, therefore, Compensation management is a crucial element to ensure that we have best talent available in the organization.
The company ensures that workforce is paid wages which meet or exceed the minimum wages laid out legally or as per government standard.
The Company will review pay and benefits annually, and will consider the business climate, financial situation, ability to pay, sales forecasts, market and competitor rates for similar jobs, individual performance, experience, length of service and internal & external equity. We would like to meet the twin objectives of being above market pay for Key position while being efficient, competitive & sustainable in our overall manpower cost. Compensation for employees will be determined based on the following parameters.
- Criticality of the Position
- Position Responsibility
- Position deliverables
- Relevant previous experience
- Performance & Competence
- Qualification
- Availability of talent in market
- Market and competitor compensation level for same Roll
- Internal Equity
- Location of Work

Annual Compensation Revision.
For all the employees in the Organization, Salary will be revised once every year. Normally the revision/Increment will take effect on 1st April each year. The increments will be linked to individual performance in accordance with an employee’s performance rating, based on Annual Appraisal. The performance year will be aligned to financial year April-March
All employees joining on or before 30th September will be eligible for revision in the ongoing financial year.
- The Company, based on the Individual Performance level indicated in the annual performance assessment, will grant annual salary revision. The recommendations of appraisers /reviewers/functional heads for this purpose will be moderated/ reviewed by the HR and same will be endorsed by HR Head/CMD.
- The rate of revision to be granted for different level of performance will depend upon the Individual Performance and business performance.
- % Revision will be based on annual revision grid prepare by HR and endorsed by HR Head/ CMD.

chapters.title: Leave Policy
chapters.text:
## Privilege Leave (Pl):
- PL Entitlement: 10 days per year.
- Maximum number of days to be carried forward per year: 30 days.
- The above accumulation of 30 days will be excluding the current year entitlement.
- Encashment: Over and above 50 days can be encashed during the service period, and all balance PL will be encashed at the time of resignation/retirement/separation at the last drawn Basic Salary.
- Credit of Leave: Leave will be credited at the beginning of the year. Any employee who joins after 1st January during the year will have PL credited on a pro-rata basis. Other terms and conditions will apply as per the Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006.
- Excess Avail: Upon leaving the organization, employees who have availed PL more than their entitlement will have the proportionate deduction made from their Gross Salary.
- Rule for availing the Leave: PL can be availed a maximum of 5 times in a year. A minimum of 1-day leave can be applied. For availing 3 or more PL, employees need to apply 1 week in advance.
- Clubbing of Leave: PL cannot be clubbed with CL, SL, Paternity Leave, or C-off.
- Intervening Weekly-off & Public Holidays during Leave period: Any weekly off or public holiday intervening the PL period shall not be considered as PL.
## Sick Leave (SL)
- Leave Entitlement: 14 days per year.
- Maximum number of days to be carried forward per year: 20 days.
- Encashment: No encashment.
- Over & above 20 days will be lapsed: The above accumulation of 20 days will be excluding the current year entitlement.
- Credit of Leave: Leave will be credited at the beginning of the year.
- Employee joining after 1st January during the Year: SL will be credited on a pro-rata basis.
- Excess Avail: Upon leaving the organization, employees who have availed SL more than their entitlement; the proportionate deduction shall be made from the Gross Salary.
- Rule for availing the Leave: 1/2-day SL can be availed. For availing 3 days or more SL at a time, employees need to produce a medical certificate along with a fitness certificate. In case of availing SL, employees must inform their Department Head/Superior/HR Department within 24 hours after proceeding on Sick Leave.
- Clubbing of Leave: Normally, SL cannot be clubbed with PL, CL, Paternity Leave, or C-off. In case of prolonged illness, PL and CL can be utilized or clubbed with SL if the employee has exhausted their SL.
- Intervening Weekly-off & Public Holidays during Leave period: Any weekly off or public holiday intervening the SL period shall be considered as SL.
## Casual Leave (CL)
- Leave Entitlement: 10 days per year.
- Maximum number of days to be carried forward per year: Nil (as carrying forward CL is not permitted under Bangladesh Labour Law).
- Encashment: Not applicable (as CL cannot be encashed under the law).
- Credit of Leave: Leave will be credited at the beginning of the year. Employees who join after January 1st will receive CL on a pro-rata basis.
- Excess Avail: Upon leaving the organization, employees who have availed CL more than their entitlement will have proportionate deductions made from their gross salary.
- Rule for availing the Leave: Half-day CL can be availed. Employees may take up to 3 days at a time, with prior approval at least one day in advance.
- Clubbing of Leave: CL cannot be clubbed with PL, SL, Paternity Leave, or Compensatory Off (C-off).
- Intervening Weekly-off & Holidays during Leave Period: Any weekly off or paid holiday falling within the CL period will count as CL.
## Maternity Leave (ML)
- Number of Days: 16 weeks (8 weeks before and 8 weeks after delivery) as per the Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006.
- Eligibility: Women employees who have completed 6 months of continuous service are eligible for fully paid maternity leave.
- Leave Conditions: Maternity leave is applicable for up to two surviving children.
- Leave Entitlement: Paternity leave is not mandated by law but may be provided as a company benefit.
- Policy: Employees are eligible for 2 days of paternity leave for the birth of up to 2 children.
## Additional Weekly Off
- Policy: Employees in managerial roles (Deputy Manager and above) may be granted 2 additional weekly offs per month as a company policy, provided it complies with the total working hour limits.
- Legal Compliance: Weekly off must be assigned in compliance with the Bangladesh Labour Act, ensuring a maximum of 48 working hours per week (excluding overtime).
## Leave Without Pay (LWP)
- Policy: LWP may be applied for when no other leave is available.
- Maximum Days: A maximum of 30 days can be availed with department head approval.
## Shift Change
- Policy:
- The monthly shift schedule should be assigned within 4 working days from the start of every month.
- Up to 3 shift changes may be permitted per month in emergencies, with prior approval from the department head.
- Compliance: Must adhere to the maximum allowable working hours under the law.

- Eligibility: Employees must have worked for at least 30 working days in a year.
- Eid Bonus: Employees are entitled to two bonuses annually, equivalent to basic salary, aligned with Eid-ul-Fitr and Eid-ul-Adha.
- Bonus Year: April 1st to March 31st.
- Minimum Bonus: As per law, 8.33% of annual basic salary must be paid.
- Salary Limit for Bonus Eligibility: Employees earning a basic salary up to Tk 15,000 are eligible.
- Payment Deadline: Bonuses must be paid within 8 months after the close of the accounting year.

## Attendance Recording and Working Hours Policy
- It is necessary for all employees to record their attendance daily so that the payroll can correctly pay salary to the employees. Through the Attendance Recording System Machines (ARS), employees can record their attendance (clock in and clock out) daily through the attendance recording machine (Face Reading/ Touch Screen Machine) provided at all the location of the Company, Factory, Offices, as per the shift timings. This policy objectives to simplify our attendance recording system while encouraging a culture of trust, integrity, and self-discipline in the organization.
- Working Days: From Saturday to Thursday
- Working Time: 8 AM to 5 PM (8.00 AM to 5.00 PM)
- Weekly Holiday: Friday
- As per Section 100 of the Bangladesh Labor Act, 2006, no worker shall be made to work more than 8 hours in a day.
- Workers are entitled to a 1-hour break after 5 continuous hours of work.
- Overtime is optional and will only be done with the consent of the worker.
- Overtime compensation: For any overtime worked, employees will receive 2 times the normal rate of basic wages, as required by the Bangladesh Labor Act, 2006.
- Workers shall not ordinarily work more than 48 hours per week. However, total hours worked in any week shall not exceed 60 hours. The average weekly working hours shall not exceed 56 hours per year.
## Weekly Rest:
- 1 day of weekly rest is mandatory after 6 consecutive working days.
- If the worker is required to work on their weekly rest day, the worker shall be entitled to compensatory leave or overtime pay as per the Bangladesh Labor Act, 2006.
## Shift Work:
- To maintain continuity of production, the company may operate on a shift system.
- The shift schedules will be provided, and the total working hours (including breaks) shall not exceed 10 hours in any given day.
- If the worker’s shift extends beyond midnight, the worker will receive a full day's leave after the shift ends, with hours worked after midnight counted as part of the previous day’s working hours.
## Attendance Compliance:
- Workers are required to record their attendance daily using the Attendance Recording System (ARS) at the company’s premises, including clocking in and clocking out as per the shift timings.
- Late arrival: Workers who arrive more than 30 minutes after the scheduled time may be refused work for the day.

chapters.title: Overtime Compensation:
chapters.text:
- Overtime will be paid at double the normal rate of basic wages, as stipulated by the Bangladesh Labor Act, 2006.
- Overtime work is voluntary, and it requires the consent of the worker.
## Team Scheduling:
- Workers will be divided into teams and assigned shifts. The authority will prepare shift schedules to ensure smooth operations.
- If a worker's shift extends beyond midnight, the worker will be granted a full day’s leave after the shift ends. The number of hours worked after midnight will be calculated as part of the previous day's working hours.
## Emergency Work and Compensation:
- In the event of a special emergency, if a worker is required to work on their weekly rest day or is deprived of leave, the worker will be granted the equivalent number of compensatory leave days as soon as possible.
## Overtime Work Eligibility:
- All adult workers employed by Arrival Fashion Limited shall not ordinarily work more than 8 (eight) hours a day.
- Workers may engage in overtime work on any day or week as specified under the Bangladesh Labor Act, 2006, with their consent.
## Overtime Allowance:
- Daily working hours exceeding 8 (eight) hours are considered overtime.
- Overtime work is optional and requires the full consent of the worker.
- Workers shall not ordinarily work more than 48 (forty-eight) hours a week. Total working hours, including overtime, must not exceed 60 (sixty) hours in a week and shall not average more than 56 (fifty-six) hours per week in a year.
## Overtime Wages:
- Overtime wages shall be paid at double the normal rate of basic wages, including applicable allowances such as festival allowances and interim wages.
- Calculation for overtime per hour: (Basic Pay ÷ 208) × 2.
## Continuity of Production Process:
- To ensure uninterrupted production, departments may operate in shifts. If a worker’s shift extends beyond midnight, they will be entitled to a full day of rest (24 continuous hours) after the end of their shift.
- The hours worked past midnight will be added to the previous day’s working hours.
## Work Period and Breaks:
- The total work period, including meal and rest breaks, shall not exceed 10 (ten) hours per day.
- A break of 1 (one) hour is provided after 5 (five) consecutive working hours.
## Special Emergency Work:
- In emergencies requiring work during weekends or depriving a worker of entitled leave, compensatory leave equal to the missed days shall be provided as soon as possible.
## Scheduling and Shift Management:
- Where all workers are required to work simultaneously, the owner or managing authority shall fix a general schedule.
- For workers whose duties vary, schedules may differ based on the nature of their work. Workers may be divided into teams, and shift schedules will be predetermined, indicating the working hours for each team.

chapters.title: Flexible working hours Policy
chapters.text:
- Eligibility: Flexible working hours are available to all full-time employees who have completed their probationary period and have demonstrated reliability and accountability in their roles, as per the provisions under the Bangladesh Labor Act, 2006.
- Core Working Hours: While flexibility is encouraged, all employees are expected to be present during core hours from 08:00 AM to 5:00 PM, ensuring adequate coverage and collaboration within teams.
- Flexible Working Arrangements: Employees may choose from various flexible working arrangements, including compressed workweeks, flexitime, or staggered shifts, subject to approval by their supervisor and based on the departmental needs. Any arrangement must align with company operations and ensure compliance with the Labor Act, 2006.
- Telecommuting: Telecommuting options are available for eligible employees, allowing them to work remotely for a portion of their scheduled hours. Telecommuting is subject to prior approval from the department head and adherence to company policies and guidelines. Employees must ensure that their work performance and output meet organizational standards while working remotely.
## Eligibility Criteria:
- Adherence to the Bangladesh Labor Act, 2006:
- It incorporates provisions for working hours and operational requirements.
- It respects employee rights while maintaining flexibility in compliance with local labor standards.
- Performance-based Criteria:
- Employee performance ratings and error rates are measurable and reflect global and local workplace standards.
- Clear Approval Processes:
- Flexible working hours require formal approval by supervisors, ensuring operational feasibility, which is consistent with workplace governance in Bangladesh.
- Communication & Coordination:
- The policy emphasizes clear communication and regular check-ins, supporting a structured approach to flexible work arrangements, even in remote or hybrid setups.

## Overtime Work and Wages Calculation:
- Workers performing overtime will receive wages at double their basic hourly rate for the additional hours.
- Overtime Wage Calculation Formula:
- Overtime per hour = (Basic Pay ÷ 208) × 2.
- This policy ensures compliance with the Bangladesh Labor Act, 2006, promoting fair and transparent working conditions for all employees.
## Terms and Conditions:
- Overtime Approval
- All overtime work must be approved in advance by the Head of Department (HOD).
- Requests for overtime must be submitted in writing.
- In exceptional circumstances, such as urgent client meetings, pressing deadlines, audits, or other critical situations, last-minute requests may be considered. The HOD will evaluate such requests on a case-by-case basis.
- Employees who work overtime without prior approval may face corrective action, as this is against company policy.
- Avoidance of Compensatory Time
- Whenever feasible, efforts should be made to adjust employees' work hours within the same workweek to prevent the accrual of compensatory time.
- Shift Change and Overtime
- Shift changes for personal reasons cannot be counted or related to overtime.

## Job Classification and Compensation Policy
- Job Classification:
- Positions in the company will be classified using a structured job evaluation system, taking into account factors such as:
- Skill level required for the position.
- Experience prerequisites for effective job performance.
- Job intricacy and decision-making responsibilities.
- Physical demands associated with the role.
- Compensation Structure:
- Each job classification will be associated with a designated base pay rate, fostering internal equity and compliance with Bangladesh labor laws and industry benchmarks.
- Market research and salary surveys may be utilized to ascertain competitive pay rates while adhering to the Minimum Wages Rules, 1961, and other relevant regulations.
- The compensation structure will ensure fairness and transparency within the organization.
## Compensation Components

- Performance Assessment: Individual performance evaluations will be conducted to evaluate employee contributions, guiding decisions on merit-based salary adjustments or advancement opportunities.

chapters.title: Equal Opportunity Policy
chapters.text:
## Purpose
With ‘Respect for Diversity’ being one of our core values, Arrival Fashion Ltd. is committed to being an equal opportunity employer in Bangladesh. This commitment is reinforced by our Corporate Business Principles and our Code of Business Conduct.
“Our success is based on our people. We treat each other with respect and dignity and expect everyone to promote a sense of personal responsibility. We recruit competent and motivated individuals who respect our values, provide equal opportunities for their development and advancement, protect their privacy, and do not tolerate any form of harassment or discrimination.”
“We embrace diversity and respect the personal dignity of our fellow employees. Arrival Fashion Ltd. respects the personal dignity, privacy, and personal rights of every employee and is dedicated to maintaining a workplace free from discrimination and harassment. Therefore, employees must not discriminate based on origin, nationality, religion, race, gender, age, marital status, or any disability, or engage in any verbal or physical harassment for any reason. Employees who feel that their workplace does not adhere to these principles are encouraged to raise their concerns with the HR Department.”
Arrival Fashion Ltd. remains committed to ensuring all professional development and promotion processes are conducted with fairness and non-discrimination, fully aligned with the labor laws and social norms of Bangladesh.
## Scope
The Equal Opportunity Policy is applicable for all job applicants and employees.
## Policy Framework
Arrival Fashion Ltd. is committed to providing equal opportunities without any discrimination on the grounds of age, color, disability, origin, nationality, religion, race, gender, or sexual orientation and prohibits any form of verbal or physical harassment based on any of the above or any other reason.
To uphold this commitment:
Respect and Dignity: All employees are personally responsible for treating each other with respect and dignity, including recognizing and respecting the rights and differences of others.
Arrival Fashion Ltd. believes that fostering mutual respect and embracing diversity is fundamental to creating a positive and productive workplace for all.
- Merit-Based Employment: Employment at Arrival Fashion Ltd. will be strictly based on merit, without consideration of irrelevant attributes or characteristics that an individual may possess.
- Development and Promotion: Opportunities for professional development and promotion will be determined by performance, ability, and potential, ensuring alignment with the needs of the business.
- Zero Tolerance for Harassment: Arrival Fashion Ltd. strictly prohibits harassment, discriminatory behavior, and victimization in the workplace. Any breaches of this policy, whether through acts of discrimination, harassment, bullying, or victimization—or through making false claims—will result in appropriate action following an investigation.
- Grievance Redressal Mechanisms: Employees experiencing discrimination, harassment, bullying, or victimization may raise their concerns with the HR department or use established grievance mechanisms like Speak Up or contact the HOD confidentially via telephone, email, or letter. All complaints will be addressed with sensitivity, fairness, and seriousness.
- Infrastructure and Accommodation: In compliance with the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act 2013 and Rules, Arrival Fashion Ltd. ensures that suitable infrastructure and reasonable accommodations are provided to employees with disabilities, enabling them to perform their duties effectively.
- Diversity and Inclusion Oversight: The company has a designated Diversity & Inclusion Council responsible for overseeing the infrastructure and facilities required for recruitment and support of Persons with Disabilities.
- Equal Opportunities for All: Arrival Fashion Ltd. is committed to ensuring that no opportunities are denied to persons from minority groups or those with disabilities, and discrimination of any kind will not be tolerated.
- Wage Equality: Promoting wage equality involves regular pay audits, addressing biases, and creating standardized pay structures. Analyzing root causes and fostering transparency ensure fairness, while periodic reviews and stakeholder engagement support continuous improvement. These actions build an inclusive culture valuing equal pay for equal work.

chapters.title: Group Personal Accident and Mediclaim Policy
chapters.text:
- The Group Personal Accident Insurance covers any accident occurring during & out-side working hours (24 hours’ coverage), which may result in death, permanent or temporary disablement. This is worldwide coverage.
- This Procedure is applicable to all employees at Arrival Fashion Ltd. All permanent employees of the company including Trainees and Workmen who are on the Company’s payroll, to provide risk coverage in case of an accident.
- This Policy provides risk coverage in case of an accident of an employee by providing the following benefits:
- Medical Expenses Reimbursement for treatment in case of Permanent or Total Temporary disablement arising out of accident.
- Accident Leave compensation or Weekly Compensation for the period of leave due to accident. (Temporary Total Disablement/or Permanent Partial Disablement as per the GPA Policy Company).
- Compensation to nominee in case of death of employee arising out of accident or Compensation to employee in case of Permanent Total Disablement or Permanent Partial Disablement.
- Other Benefits.
## Reimbursement and Benefit:
- The amount & type of compensation payable will be dependent on the extent of disability. Various reimbursements applicable under the scheme are:
- Reimbursement of expenses incurred toward medical treatment depending upon the policy. In case of Temporary Total Disablement, reimbursement, depending upon scheme of the Insurance Policy.
- In case of death of employee due to accident, the beneficiary/nominee will be paid the total sum assured. The total sum assured will be depending upon the Insurance Policy.
- In case of permanent disablement, the benefits will be paid to employee depending upon the kind of disablement, as decided by the Insurance Authorities.
- If an employee suffers an accident in course of employment or connected with work (this include travelling from residence to office and back, travelling for official work), and is required to take leave of absence & medical treatment.
- The company will grant him paid ‘Accident Leave’ for period of temporary disability and reimburse all medical expenses at actual.
- In all such case any insurance claim amount received under this Group Personal Accident Policy (GPA) towards the leave compensation & medical expenses of the concerned employee will be retained by the Company.
- If an employee suffers an accident outside the course of employment or in a situation not connected with employment and is required to take leave of absence & medical treatment.
- All such accident leave will be leave without pay & medical expenses will be borne by the employee.
- In all such case any insurance claim amount claimed under this Group Personal Accident Policy (GPA) towards the leave compensation & medical expenses of the employee will be reimbursed to the employees as per the said GPA Policy.
- Other Benefits are as per the GPA Policy taken from the Insurance Company.
- The all the benefits under this policy will be as per the GPA Policy taken by the Insurance claim. Complete Group Personal Accident Policy details & procedure for claim & will be as per the GPA policy taken from the Insurance Company.
- If there is any dispute regarding interpretation or meaning of any word or clause of this policy or any discrepancy in types of benefits mentioned in this Policy or the benefits offered by the insurance company, then Original GPA Policy issued by the Insurance Company shall prevail.

chapters.title: Waste Disposal Policy
chapters.text:
- The authorities of Arrival Fashion Limited follow a strict policy to maintain a hygienic working environment by properly disposing of wastes from the factory production process and other solid or liquid wastes.
- The factory has a separate room for keeping the waste from the production process (coots, scraps of cloth, used yarn, plastic pieces of hangers or other waste) so that it does not cause pollution or disruption of the working environment of the factory, from where it is necessary. The factory area is removed by the designated false tradesmen following proper procedures.
- When a cloth is cut in the cutting section of the factory, before cutting the cloth is measured according to style and after cutting the cutting area, the jute and the remaining cloth are properly cleaned.
- Metal materials used in factories such as cutters, scissors, needles used in sewing and other metal materials become unusable.
- Stored in factory store, arranged for removal later. Electrical equipment such as 4 pieces of wire, broken/fused tube lights, broken switches and other unusable electrical equipment should be stored separately in specific containers and Removal is arranged.
- When any type of wood material is broken or unusable, it is stored and disposed of separately.
- Also, all types of paper, pens, markers, plastic materials, polythene, paper-made cartons, etc. used in the office and production floor are stored and disposed of separately after use or when unusable.
- At mid-day meal, the dust and garbage collected from pick-dani, production floor, factory surroundings, walkways etc. are arranged to be thrown into the dustbin by the cleaner.
- Effluent or garbage from toilets, urinals, lavatories goes directly to the safety tank of the factory.
- Adequate water flow is provided to each waste pipe and drain, so that no obstruction is created in the removal of waste.
- All water use areas are connected to factory main drains and municipal drains are connected to these drains in a proper manner so that the water used in the factory can be discharged properly.
- The main drains of the factory are made deep and wide enough to prevent overflow during removal of water or dirt.
- Burnt lubricating oil of generators, oil used in sewing machines are properly changed and preserved, later disposal is arranged.
- The sludge of ETP is properly stored in time and then the wastes are disposed of without causing any harm to the environment.
- Factory cleaners ensure a hygienic working environment by keeping the factory clean at all times by properly removing all solid, liquid and other wastes generated by the manufacturing process in the factory.
## Health & Hygiene Policy:
- If someone suddenly falls ill in the factory, he is given first aid and the doctor on duty is informed.
- The first aid box is checked daily and the inspection book is signed.
- Medicine log and accidental log are properly maintained.
- It is checked whether the patient carrying 'stretcher' is in the designated place.
- Drinking water is ensured to be pure and checked that each worker uses individual water bottles.
- At least 2 times the toilet and waste basket are cleaned and the check list is signed. Toilet flush, basin tap, water filter are checked for proper functioning.
- Toilets are checked for soap and odour-free toilets.
- Clean towels are checked for hand drying.
- If someone in the factory falls ill, his neighbouring colleagues will immediately inform the first aider. In case of failure to take necessary first aid measures, inform the nurse, if the nurse fails to take necessary measures, take it to the doctor and if the doctor fails to take the necessary measures, take it to the contracted hospital of the factory.
## Chemical safety policy
- Arrival Fashion Limited follows a specific procedure regarding chemical substances in accordance with the prevailing labor laws of the country of the employees and the policies adopted by the company. Committed to ensure safety of chemicals in light of statutory labor laws of the country.
- There should be a list/list of chemicals used in the factory.
- Chemicals should be stored in a specific place as per the list.
- Store containers with chemicals on secondary containment with sand and shall keep the sand dry by changing it as necessary. Know about chemical usage rules and precautionary instructions.
- Adequate training should be given to the chemical user on chemical usage rules and precautions.
- No chemicals should be stored and used except in the prescribed place and manner.
- Use all protective equipment as directed when handling chemicals.
- To identify the chemical, the chemical container should have a level attached. Levelling the area where the chemical will be located according to the name of the chemical.
- have to do Before using chemicals, it must be ensured that the correct chemical is being used for the correct job.

chapters.title: Fire Safety Policy
chapters.text:
- "Fire" is one of the main enemies of the garment industry which can instantly destroy the garment and its manufacturing plant, ending the precious life of the workers. To prevent this terrible fire, Arrival Fashion Ltd. has a written strategy called "Fire Safety Policy" which is as follows Given: The exit door from every room in the factory is bolted during working hours in the factory and all doors are easily opened from inside.
- There are 3 (three) emergency exits for emergency exits in case of fire other than normal exits and the exits are clearly marked in red ink in large size and easy to understand signals in the language understandable by most of the workers. There are exits to every room in the factory building and they are located in such a way that every person can reach the exit from his place of work with reasonable ease and ease. Factory-built floors, stairs, walkways and bridges that are solidly built.
- Maintained and have suitable handrails on stairs, walkways and gangways.
- Stairways in the factory are constructed of fire-resistant material and are not less than 45" wide. Emergency evacuation maps with "I'm here" signs are posted at appropriate places in the factory showing all locations in the factory in a language understood by the workers. Every worker employed in the factory is informed of fire. Effective and easily listenable.
- There is a warning system on the way. Constant communication with the local fire brigade unit is maintained so that necessary measures can be taken quickly to the factory in case of fire.
- The factory has 2 fire hose reel pipes per floor. The factory has a sufficient number of portable fire extinguishers made of carbon-dioxide, dry powder carbon tetrachloride.
- Each portable fire extinguisher is placed in a location approved by the inspector and each fire extinguisher meets the appropriate standard specification. Sufficient spare charges for fire extinguishers are kept in factory. A maximum of spare charges are always stocked and ready to be used when needed.
- One fourth of the workers employed in each department in the factory have been trained in the use of portable fire extinguishers and notices regarding the use of fire extinguishers have been posted at appropriate places in Bengal. "Fire drills" are organized in the factory once every two months to make the training on the use of fire extinguishers more effective.
- Always performing duties with humility and gentleness.
- Always use identification card and uniform while working. Every guard and supervisor engaged in security work must be informed of local laws relating to security.
- Constant monitoring of factory assets.
- If an employee enters the factory after the specified time, write the employee's card number in the prescribed form and give it to the concerned officer.
- After entering the factory, no employee shall leave without the permission of the authority.
- Authorities must identify and meet outsiders or visitors
- Must be informed and entry without permission of authority is strictly prohibited.
- Every visitor or outsider authorized by the authority shall issue a visiting card. In this case one must be polite and elegant with the visitor. It is specially noted that in case of special guests, the supervisor on duty has to supervise.
- Any kind of accident, commotion, noise and personal or company damage should be immediately reported to the concerned officer and the incident should be recorded.
- In the case of hiring employees in the factory or conducting day-to-day operations with the employees.
- Recommendations or nepotism of guards are not acceptable in any case. Besides, accepting any kind of money, gift or benefit is a punishable offence. Certain security personnel engaged for the safety of factory assets and personnel
- No one can carry any kind of weapon other than that. In this case, special training should be arranged for those who will be allowed to keep weapons. Also, no worker will be allowed to carry any personal weapon.
- Goods carried by the workers will be checked during factory holidays as per the rules prescribed by the authorities. If a physical search is ever required, it will be done by a person of the same sex.
- Factory workers shall not be subjected to physical or mental torture under any circumstances. A person engaged in security work performs routine daily tasks
- Will not use muscle power in case. If muscles are ever used in self-defence or in an emergency, appropriate explanation must be given to the security personnel involved.
- Everyone engaged in security work should be trained in security policies and harassment and bullying-free policies. Closed circuit cameras (CCTV) in the factory are constantly monitoring and alert.
- Maintained and have suitable handrails on stairs, walkways and gangways.

chapters.text:
## Objective:
To outline the training program approach and describe the procedure to execute it. This training program ensures that employees receive adequate training , their areas of work and that the training is documented. It provides a procedure to identify, plan, execute and document the training for personnel engaged in garment manufacturing and their support activities.
## Scope:
This procedure is applicable to initial and ongoing technical training of new and existing employees at manufacturing sites of Arrival Fashion Ltd. It covers both permanent and contractual staff.
## Site Training Coordinator:
- Ensuring the completion of On-job training of the new employees prior to attending to their routine work.
- Ensuring periodic training to the existing employees.
- Developing Training Plan for Functional training.
- Ensuring the site trainer pool is adequately staffed, through periodic identification and qualification of trainers.
- Facilitating development of training modules and delivering training courses.
- Facilitating identification and development of subject matter experts (SMEs) at site(s) for cGMP, functional and SOP trainings.
- Playing all site administrator roles, along with tracking of employee curriculum progress and triggering escalation wherever needed in AFL Training Management System (AFLTMS).
## Department Training Coordinator (DTC):
- Facilitating mapping of SOP specific training requirements for respective functions and support trainer/ SME qualification activities.
- Tracking & monitoring training progress along with reporting, and escalation, as needed, to Site training coordinator/Department Head.
- Playing department training coordinator role in AFL Training Management System (AFLTMS).
## nstructor/Subject Matter Experts:
- Will train employees and share associated knowledge.
- Playing trainer role in AFL Training Information Management System (AFLTIMS).
## Human Resources:
- Coordinating and ensuring the completion of onsite and offsite Training Program for all the new employees.
- Playing HR Coordinator role in AFL Training Management System (AFLTMS).
## All Employees
- Completion of all the assigned learnings within the stipulated time frame.
- Playing Learner role in AFLTMS.
## Procedure:
- Process that involves acquiring knowledge, sharpening of skills, concepts, rules, to enhance the performance of employees. Training is an activity leading to skilled behaviour.
## Training Need Identification (TNI):
- Process that involves identifying, documenting and assigning the trainings required for an employee job role to acquire and/or upgrade their technical knowledge. This is in order to effectively execute their core job responsibilities, and/ or those which contribute to employee’s personal development.
## Training Management System:
- Training Information Management System (TMS) is a software application for the administration, imparting training, documentation, tracking, and reporting of training programs – classroom, online/offline training events, e-learning programs and training content.
## Training of New Permanent Employees:
- All new permanent employees engaged in manufacturing, quality control, warehousing, engineering and quality assurance functions etc. shall get basic induction training at the time of joining to the organization as part of employee on-boarding exercise. Employees shall undergo site induction trainings.
## nduction Training:
- Induction training is carried out. Through this introduction or orientation, induction training is given to the workers on all relevant matters including calculation of pay/overtime, other regulations, factory canteen, etc. to increase their awareness. Workers cannot leave the workplace without permission during work, workers must follow all rules regarding arrival and departure as per the work schedule. Factory property/goods shall not be deliberately destroyed or damaged. If you are engaged in factory/establishment/anti-state activities or subversive activities;
- Authorities can take appropriate action according to law.
- No activities against the order of the factory shall be carried out, if it is customary
- Necessary action will be taken as per labor law.
- After proper completion of the mentioned activities, the petitioner is given basic training about the required content of Bangladesh Labor Act 2006 Amendment 2023, the prevailing policies of the organization and the rules of buying and selling of globally established buyer organizations.
## Basics of Good Manufacturing Practices:
- Each new joiner / existing employees engaged in manufacturing, quality control, warehousing, engineering and quality assurance functions etc. in the organization shall be provided training on basic modules of manufacturing process. This will include providing awareness on related regulations and its expectation on Manufacturing Practices.

- Training workshops and seminars specifically tailored to address the needs and challenges faced by women in the workplace are conducted regularly.

## Grievance Mechanism and Remediation Procedure
## Objective
The Grievance Redressal procedure at Arrival Fashion Ltd. aims to reinforce the organization’s commitment towards providing fair and equitable work opportunities to all employees. The objective of the grievance resolution process is to provide employees with an easily accessible mechanism for settlement of their individual grievances.
## Scope and Applicability
This policy applies to all employees, workers, internal & external stakeholders and subcontractors of Arrival Fashion Ltd. and those of Partner organizations who are in a relationship with Arrival Fashion Ltd.
Not all grievances are related to HR. Grievance covers a wider area in the Organization, particularly those which are not directly related to or in the employee’s immediate work area and people, but, in other areas which, though not frequented very often, they necessitate interaction for work purposes or for co-existence in the workplace by the employee. These areas can relate to Cafeteria, Transport, Office maintenance, Administration, infrastructure, lighting, air-conditioning, WFH support, etc.
This policy aims to focus on non-HR related areas, with the resolution responsibility involving the line manager of the department concerned. HR is certainly kept in the loop since the locus is around the employee and the incident.
HR related grievances are covered in Code of Conduct Policy, POSH Policy, Employee relationships Policy, Violence at workplace Policy, EEO&AD policy, Maternity benefits Policy, etc
Arrival Fashion Ltd. will endeavour to address the grievance to the best possible extent as far as it is feasible, within its scope, is reasonable & has a larger impact to other employees, within legal / statutory ambit and is cost effective.
Arrival Fashion Ltd. reserves the right to reject, cancel or postpone any grievance without assigning any reason whatsoever.
## Policy/Process
## Policy Statement
The policy is developed to provide mechanism to report Grievances related environment, labour human rights, ethics, sustainable procurement for following matter & based on analysis and investigation define action against the same through committee and apply remediation measures:

- POSH Policy,

- Grievance arising out of termination/dismissal

chapters.title: Grievance Redressal Procedure
chapters.text:
- The following process should be followed for expressing and seeking redressal to a grievance
- Employees may communicate their grievance in writing to their manager first while at the same time, addressing a copy to the concerned department Head. In case the grievance involves the Manager, then the employee can contact the Manager, while simultaneously copying the concerned.
- The concerned manager must immediately acknowledge receipt of the grievance in writing, informing the employee of the receipt of grievance and inviting the employee for a formal meeting.
- If the grievance pertains to the same function where the employee works, the Manager has to review and resolve the same based on the feasibility or commit to a timeline by which the same could be resolved as per dependency on other departments / functions / vendors or factors.
- In other cases, Manager may consult with the concerned departments or functions to which the grievance pertains to for their action or feedback and revert to the employee with a course of action / solution within 7 working days from the date of receipt of grievance.
- In case an employee is not satisfied with the solution, the employee may choose to represent the grievance to Department Head (or to a LT member), if the grievance concerns the Department Head.
- The Leadership Team (LT) member will convey their decision to the aggrieved employee through the concerned department manager within 5 days of receipt of the complaint. If, however, the LT is of the view that the matter should be referred to the Grievance Resolution Committee, they may do so
- The Grievance Resolution Committee consists of a minimum of three members from the Leadership Team and the concerned department Manager and any manager except from his or her own manager. The Grievance Resolution Committee (as mentioned below) will provide an opportunity to the aggrieved employee and the concerned person involved in the grievance, to present their concern. The Grievance Resolution Committee will include representatives from other teams to ensure fair and faster resolution.
[table]
| Name | Designation | Email |
| Alvi Islam | Director | alvi@arrivalfashion.com; |
| Mainuddin Sarker | Head HR and Admin | compliance.bhaluka@arrivalfashion.com; |
| KH. Shakhawat Hossain Shishir | Manager | shishir@arrivalfashion.com; |
- The Grievance Resolution Committee will give their recommendation to the LT within 4 working days. The LT will take a decision based on this recommendation and communicate their decision through the concerned department Manager to the aggrieved employee within 15 working days from commencement of inquiry
- Grievances will be treated with utmost confidentiality and sensitivity
- Human Resources shall maintain a record all grievances referred to the Grievance Resolution Committee, number of grievances settled/ pending and report to the Senior Management Team on a quarterly basis
## Gross misconduct
In case the grievance by an employee leads to discovery of gross conduct by another employee(s) or associates or vendors of Arrival Fashion Ltd., appropriate action will be taken by HR, while the identity of the complainant will not be disclosed in any manner or forum.
The list provided below is illustrative but not exhaustive, and should be deemed that any other conduct not falling within the purview of what is stated below is akin to gross misconduct; the LT will exercise the authority in consultation with the Grievance Redressal Committee to determine gross misconduct depending on the circumstances of each case
- Fraud
- Deliberate falsification of records
- Embezzlement
- Theft
- Intimidation, harassment, threats or acts of violence.
- Misuse or misappropriation of position or benefits.
- Wilful damage to an organization’s assets, including those of its employees, partners, other stakeholders.
- Disparagement or defamation of the Organization, its employees, partners, or other stakeholders
- Taking or giving bribes or any other illegal gratification, including sexual gratification
- Serious incapability due to being under the influence of alcohol or being under the influence of illegal drugs at the workplace and during working hours.
- Serious negligence which causes unacceptable loss, damage, or injury
- Serious act of insubordination
- Deception or inappropriate access to private and/ or confidential Company records and/ or information without authorization or need-to-know.
## Appeals
An employee who wishes to appeal against a disciplinary decision must do so within five working days. The Grievance Redressal Committee will hear all appeals and will make are commendation to the LT. Where felt appropriate and in very serious cases, the LT may further consult the Board. The LTs decision will be final and communicated in writing to the employee by the concerned department Manager. At the appeal, any disciplinary penalty imposed will be reviewed.

## Policy Provisions Contents
## Preamble
AFL Ltd values the use of information technology in supporting the mission of the Company. Our business services gain strength and currency from our research activities, strong industry links and our international nature. AFL has strong engagements with partnerships from both local and global communities allowing AFL to share knowledge, debate and research outcomes.
In this context, AFL information, whether managed and residing on AFL resources or held in trust and managed by third parties or business partners, is an important asset that must be protected. Any person or organization that uses or holds in trust these assets have a responsibility to maintain and safeguard them.
AFL is committed to preserving the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information regardless of the form it takes - electronic or non-electronic. Improper use of information resources may result in harm to the AFL Ltd and its mission of creating value through superior, apparel products and operate as a responsible company.
## Policy Statements
## Data Backup
Data Backups are primarily a preventative measure to protect against loss of data resulting from system failure (disaster or other), virus/malware attack, system or human error.
Backups are an essential control and safeguard to ensure availability of AFL information being stored, processed or transmitted via information technology communication systems.
Statement: Data must be backed up on a regular basis, protected from unauthorized access or modification during storage, and available to be recovered in a timely manner in the event of incident or disaster.

## Data Security
AFL supports an extensively broad and complex data landscape. Based on appropriate data classification and handling guidelines, this policy and associated standard ensures that appropriate controls are implemented for the confidentiality and integrity of sensitive data.
Statement: Encryption techniques must be used for protecting sensitive data during transmission and storage.
See Work Instructions in for encryption procedure, SOPs, Encrypted data flow for Email, ERP, FTP, other applications.
Control: Encryption Policy defined for Storage drive of End Points.
## Security Incident Management
Provides preventive, corrective and detective measures, ensuring a consistent and effective approach to the management of information security incidents, including communication of events and weaknesses, such as breach of access.
Well, designed, understood tools and processes will help contain, preserve (legal / forensic purposes) and limit any damage resulting from a security incident.
Statement: Incident detection mechanisms such as security event logging and antivirus must be implemented for all IT systems. All potential security incidents must be handled appropriately following a formalized security incident handling process.
Control: Security Incident Management at AFL (Scope, Vulnerability assessment, Tools used, Handling security incident, Impact assessment, User awareness, Classification of Data, Risk Management scope, ownership and mitigation defined across all assets).
## ulnerability Management
All systems are susceptible to vulnerability (weakness) and therefore under constant threat from malicious exploitation that may result in the compromise of confidentiality, integrity or availability of AFL information or systems, potentially resulting in productivity, reputational or financial loss.
Vulnerability management involves alerting and responding to identified and potential violations or security threats in a timely, measured and prioritized (risk based) manner, in order to prevent or limit the damage. Vulnerability management is considered a preventive and corrective measure.
Statement: Security patch and vulnerability management processes must be in place to identify, prioritize and remediate security vulnerabilities on IT assets.
